gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: The photographer ___ camera was damaged is claiming compensation.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' shows that the camera belongs to the photographer; 'who's' means 'who is'.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.
